structured.explanation: This test checks that when a caller changes a nested dict in a mapping schema after passing it to normalize_schema, the router-side parser still accepts an integer count and rejects a string one. Without the deepcopy, the parser shares the caller's nested dicts, so `{"count": 3}` would be rejected. That assertion is also why `spec.json_schema` alone can't catch the defect: SchemaSpec deep-copies it in __post_init__ either way. # mutation-pin: REQ_STRUCTURED_SCHEMA_CONTRACT SM-9C5C73BC
from __future__ import annotations

import jsonschema
import pytest

from llm_router._internal.capabilities.schema import normalize_schema

pytestmark = pytest.mark.verification_kind("unit")


@pytest.mark.verifies("REQ_STRUCTURED_SCHEMA_CONTRACT[revision==2]")
def test_mapping_schema_validation_ignores_later_caller_nested_mutation() -> None:
    count_property = {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0}
    schema = {
        "title": "ItemCount",
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"count": count_property},
        "required": ["count"],
    }

    spec = normalize_schema(schema)
    count_property["type"] = "string"

    assert spec.json_schema["properties"]["count"]["type"] == "integer"
    assert spec.parse('{"count": 3}') == {"count": 3}
    with pytest.raises(
        jsonschema.ValidationError,
        match=r"'three' is not of type 'integer'",
    ):
        spec.parse('{"count": "three"}')
